definitions.explanation: A sticky substance used for joining things together.
A substance used to stiffen fabric.

examples.japanese: {糊|のり}で{紙|かみ}を{貼|は}り{合|あ}わせる。
ワイシャツに{糊|のり}をきかせる。
{封筒|ふうとう}の{糊|のり}がはがれた。
examples.english: The glue on the envelope came off.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{糊|のり}で{手|て}をべたべたにしてしまった。
examples.english: The child got their hands all sticky with glue.

examples.japanese: {工作|こうさく}の{時間|じかん}に{糊|のり}を{使|つか}って{色紙|いろがみ}を{貼|は}り{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: During craft time, we used glue to paste colored paper together.

examples.japanese: {糊|のり}のきいたシャツは{気持|きも}ちがいい。
クリーニング{店|てん}で{糊付|のりづ}けを{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I asked the dry cleaner to starch my clothes.

examples.japanese: {浴衣|ゆかた}に{糊|のり}をつけてパリッとさせる。
examples.english: Starch the yukata to make it crisp.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{洗濯|せんたく}した{着物|きもの}にいつも{糊|のり}をきかせていた。
examples.english: My grandmother always starched her kimono after washing them.

examples.japanese: {糊|のり}がきつすぎると、{生地|きじ}が{固|かた}くなって{着|き}にくい。
examples.english: If you use too much starch, the fabric becomes stiff and uncomfortable to wear.

notes:
{糊|のり} refers to paste, glue, or starch. It's traditionally made from rice or wheat starch.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {糊|のり}で{貼|は}る (to paste with glue)
- {糊|のり}をつける (to apply glue)
- {糊付|のりづ}け (starching, pasting)
- {糊|のり}がきいている (well-starched, stiff)

NOTE: Not to be confused with {海苔|のり} (seaweed/nori for sushi), which has the same reading but different kanji.

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {接着剤|せっちゃくざい} (adhesive, general term)
- スティックのり (glue stick)
